observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard: south is a pink ringed worm seen end-on, with a round toothed maw at the bottom, rows of clawed limbs down both sides, and the body narrowing upward to a small spiked knob. East is a tall S-arch profile: a long tail with a spiked tip lies on the ground, the body rears up, and the front hooks forward with an open toothed sucker maw. About eight clawed limbs hang from the underside. North is a narrow, symmetric dorsal view of the ringed body with claws along both sides, narrowing to the spiked tail knob at the bottom. It has no face.
observed.south.png: Pink, wrinkled, ringed body with a circular maw ringed with cream teeth at the bottom centre, flanked by two large dark-purple claws. About five pairs of clawed limbs fan out from the sides. The body recedes upward and narrows to a spiked ball at the top, so it reads like a prone worm seen from above and in front, not the reared arch. Painterly, no keyline, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A side profile with wet, creased, dusky-rose skin. The tail lies on the ground at the left with a spiked tip. The body rises into a tall hunched arch, and the head curls forward to the right with an open round toothed sucker. Many curved, glossy, dark-purple claws hang from the ventral side. Painterly and realistic, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The back of a ringed pink worm, symmetric, with about six pairs of claws along both sides and the tail tapering to a spiked knob at the bottom. No face or eyes. The body is drawn as a long, flat, vertical strip with no visible rear arch, so it reads largely as a dorsal plan view.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the worm fills about one cell, roughly as tall as the vanilla human beside it. At 32 px it still reads as a pink, arched, clawed worm, smaller than the human.

subject: RSW_LavaFlea__LavaFlea_j

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. All three show the same dark maroon armoured arthropod at about the same height. Each has a domed, segmented carapace with a thin orange rim light and stands high on four long, thin, jointed, claw-tipped legs plus two smaller front legs. South is a front view with two glowing red eyes and a trunk. East is a side profile with the head low and forward. North is the rounded rear.
observed.south.png: Front view. The domed carapace is made of overlapping plates. Under it sits a low, wrinkled head with two glowing red-orange eyes, a segmented trunk-like proboscis hanging down the middle, and small curved mandibles on each side. Two short front legs are tucked under the face. Four long spidery legs splay wide, with knobby joints and pointed claw tips. The belly is well off the ground. The cut-out is clean.
observed.east.png: Side profile. The body is egg-shaped and hump-backed, with glossy overlapping dark plates running back from the neck. It ends abruptly at the rear with no tail. The head is low and forward, wrinkled, with one glowing eye, a downward-curved segmented proboscis and small mandibles. Two smaller front legs sit under the head. Four long stilt legs end in claws. Orange rim light runs along the top edge. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Rounded, domed back plates end in a bulbous rear segment. No face, no eyes, no tail. The four long legs splay to the sides and the two small front legs are just visible between them. Same palette and size as the other facings. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about as tall as the vanilla human and roughly twice as wide. At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark domed body on spidery legs, clearly separate from the ground, and much larger than the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: two glowing eyes, the proboscis and the mandibles.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the domed rear plates and the rounded back end, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled camera; the legs and belly clearance are visible, so none is top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 0%, and the panels look the same size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same palette, plates and leg count on every facing; the small front legs and the head turn correctly with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: A large arthropod mount with an armoured shell and lava-glow accents is clearly legible.

ALIEN.seen: The body suggests a tick, but the glowing eyes, elephant-trunk proboscis, stilt legs with the belly high off the ground, and the size together make it read as alien.

CANON.seen: All present: domed hump-backed body with no tail; six legs (four long, two small); glossy overlapping plates; dark maroon hide with legs the same colour; glowing eyes as the brightest element; orange rim light; wrinkled low head with a segmented proboscis and mandibles; no antennae; claw-tipped knobby legs.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic texturing on the plates and joints. Not cel-shaded, cute or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: A bespoke painting matching the canon description; nothing like vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs with no ground or shadow. The orange rim glow sits on the body edges as intended, not as a halo.

SCALE.seen: As tall as the human and wider, which is a plausible juvenile of a 4–5 m mount (drawSize 1.5).

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a dark dome on splayed legs, clearly apart from the ground.
